stages.title: CONCEPTUAL METHOD: WHAT PROBLEM IS BEING ASKED?
stages.terms: [THESIS] The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.
stages.mechanism: [THESIS] The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.
stages.consequence: Evil can rebut or undercut a proof, but this session does not repeat the proofs.
stages.trap: A modal defence can answer the first while leaving the other three largely untouched.
stages.answer: The problem of evil is not one argument but a family of challenges generated by the relation among a divine profile, the facts of suffering and wrongdoing, and norms governing what a good agent would permit.

stages.title: CLASSICAL FORMULATION AND MACKIE'S LOGICAL PROBLEM
stages.terms: [VERDICT] Mackie's argument remains pedagogically decisive because it forces the theist to state the hidden moral and modal assumptions.
stages.mechanism: The dilemma is transmitted in later discussion, prominently through Lactantius, and Hume's Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion gives a celebrated modern formulation through Philo.
stages.consequence: The logical debate therefore turns on whether those bridging premises are unrestricted.
stages.trap: Omnipotence means power to do what is logically possible, not power to instantiate contradictions.
stages.answer: The familiar questions - whether God is willing but unable, able but unwilling, or both able and willing while evil exists - are commonly labelled the Epicurean paradox.

stages.title: PLANTINGA'S FREE WILL DEFENCE
stages.terms: If so, God's inability to actualize freedom-with-guaranteed-goodness is not lack of omnipotence, because the proposed object is not a feasible world God can strongly actualize.
stages.mechanism: If so, God's inability to actualize freedom-with-guaranteed-goodness is not lack of omnipotence, because the proposed object is not a feasible world God can strongly actualize.
stages.consequence: If God causally determines every significantly free choice to be right, the choice is not libertarianly free in relation to God.
stages.trap: [OBJECTION] Why could God not create free persons who always freely choose the good, as the blessed might in heaven?
stages.answer: The defence is strongest for moral evil.

stages.title: EVIDENTIAL EVIL: ROWE, PROBABILITY AND SKEPTICAL THEISM
stages.terms: Skeptical theists challenge our entitlement to infer from "no reason we can see" to "probably no reason." Wykstra's CORNEA-style principle asks whether, if the proposed good existed, it is reasonable to expect that we would discern it.
stages.mechanism: We should prevent suffering because we lack authority to assume an unknown justifying plan.
stages.consequence: The point is comparative likelihood, not a numerical probability assignment.
stages.trap: The case is illustrative, not a claim that one event alone deductively disproves God.
stages.answer: Evidential force depends on a noseeum move: "We see no justifying reason; therefore there probably is none." Such reasoning is strong when observers would likely detect the relevant reason if it existed, as when looking for an elephant in a small room.

stages.title: CLASSICAL THEODICIES AND DEFENCES
stages.terms: Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.
stages.mechanism: Augustine treats evil as a privation of good arising through created freedom, not as a positive substance created by God.
stages.consequence: [QUALIFICATION] What it preserves or explains: It addresses moral and natural evil within one developmental framework and explains why God is not overwhelmingly evident.
stages.trap: [THESIS] Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.
stages.answer: Created being is good insofar as it has being; evil is not a positive substance made by God but a privation, corruption or disorder of a due good.

stages.title: NON-CLASSICAL THEISMS AND REVISED DIVINE ATTRIBUTES
stages.terms: Open theism holds that future free acts are genuinely open and known by God as possibilities rather than settled facts.
stages.mechanism: Divine action is persuasive rather than coercive, not merely because God voluntarily self-limits but because unilateral control is metaphysically unavailable.
stages.consequence: God is not the author of evil and receives the world's suffering in divine experience.
stages.trap: Reality consists in becoming actualities with their own measure of self-determination; God supplies persuasive possibilities but cannot simply coerce every event.
stages.answer: Whitehead is the metaphysical source; Hartshorne argues against classical omnipotence; David Ray Griffin develops process theodicy; John Cobb systematizes process theology.

stages.title: EXISTENTIAL EVIL, PROTEST AND HORRENDOUS EVILS
stages.terms: It should not be reduced to a neat punishment theory.
stages.mechanism: [THESIS] Horrendous evils are participation in which gives a person prima facie reason to doubt whether their life can be a great good to them.
stages.consequence: [THESIS] Existential approaches ask not only whether a proposition is coherent but what stance is humanly and morally possible before suffering.
stages.trap: They are not substitutes for formal argument; they test its existential and ethical adequacy.
stages.answer: Existential approaches ask not only whether a proposition is coherent but what stance is humanly and morally possible before suffering.

stages.title: INDIAN AND NON-WESTERN FRAMEWORKS
stages.terms: Indian traditions do not share one answer because they disagree about creator, self, world, karma (morally consequential action) and liberation.
stages.mechanism: Indian traditions do not share one answer because they disagree about creator, self, world, karma (morally consequential action) and liberation.
stages.consequence: [THESIS] Indian traditions do not share one answer because they disagree about creator, self, world, karma and liberation.
stages.trap: Nyaya (school of logic and realism): Ishvara (Lord or personal God) can administer unseen karmic potency and cosmic order; God is not an arbitrary author but a just allocator.
stages.answer: Karma (morally consequential action) is structurally strong on distribution but morally dangerous when converted into retrospective certainty about a victim.

stages.title: HARD CASES AND META-LEVEL CRITIQUES
stages.terms: Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.
stages.mechanism: [THESIS] Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.
stages.consequence: The 2024 PYQ is correct that the problem is concept-dependent, but suffering remains philosophically and religiously significant in every framework.
stages.trap: [VERDICT] The 2024 PYQ is correct that the problem is concept-dependent, but suffering remains philosophically and religiously significant in every framework.
stages.answer: Animal suffering is a central evidential challenge because predation, disease, parasitism and extinction precede human agency and often seem unrelated to moral growth.

stages.title: COMPARATIVE SYNTHESIS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS
stages.terms: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.
stages.mechanism: Theodicies should be compared through the divine attribute revised, the evil explained, the residual case and the moral cost of the explanation.
stages.consequence: Protest: need not be unbelief; Job-like protest can occur within a relationship.
stages.trap: Agents must prevent avoidable suffering because they are not entitled to assume it is necessary.
stages.answer: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.
